subject: POC hands-on load sprint — scheduling, runbook & success criteria
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC kickoff + hands-on load window (requirements & availability)

Hi Rishi/Monica,

Thanks for the quick intro last week — Acme Health is ready to book the hands-on POC and run a short load sprint to validate throughput and latency before contracting. High-level asks: 
- 2.5 hour working session (walkthrough + prompt review + routing) + 3 hour load window the following day for throughput profiling.
- Target sustained throughput: ~150 req/s (avg), spike to 300 req/s for 1m bursts.
- Latency SLOs: p95 < 300ms for the primary model path.
- We need runbook and test-harness review (our infra team will want the exact connection steps).

Attached is our requirements doc (acme_poc_requirements.pdf). Please confirm who from Redwood should be on the call (ops/eng) and share your availability next week.

Proposed dates: Oct 3–4 (US time). Open to earlier if you have capacity.

Thanks,
Lara Chen
Program Manager, Integrations
Acme Health

Attachment: acme_poc_requirements.pdf
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Sep 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff + hands-on load window (requirements & availability)

Hi Lara —

Thanks for the detail and the requirements doc. Monica and I can own the kickoff and the hands-on run; I also recommend looping Dylan Brooks (load ops) to help run the throughput windows and the test harness (he's cc'd below in a follow-up).

We can do Oct 3–4 as proposed. Tentative plan:
- Oct 3: 2.5h hands-on session (prompt review, routing policies, KV/prefix caching walkthrough, runbook read-through)
- Oct 4: 3h load window (staged traffic, steady-state + spike runs, real-time metrics and logs)

Couple of quick questions so we can prep the runbook update:
1) Will your infra team provide a NAT/egress IP allowlist for the staging cluster or do we need to provide a jump-host?
2) Which model variant do you want to prioritize for latency (accurate vs quantized)?
3) Any tokens/secrets we should expect for the test harness (we can generate ephemeral keys on our side if preferred).

I'll prepare a draft runbook (POC-Runbook-v1) and a throughput matrix for the load plan and share an updated PDF before the session. If Oct 3 works, what times (PST) are best for your team?

Best,
Rishi
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara@acmehealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Sep 2028 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff + hands-on load window (requirements & availability)

Hi Lara —

Quick heads up: I have a calendar conflict the morning of Oct 3 and would prefer to shift the hands-on to the afternoon (13:00–15:30 PST). If that doesn't work for your team, we can move the session to Oct 2 afternoon instead.

Also happy to run the prompt-review portion — can you share a few sample prompts ahead of time so we can validate prompt routing and prefix caching behavior?

Thanks,
Monica
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Lara Chen <lara@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Sep 2028 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff + hands-on load window (requirements & availability)

Thanks Rishi/Monica — afternoon on Oct 3 (13:00–15:30 PST) works for us. We'll plan the load window Oct 4 09:00–12:00 PST.

Answers to your questions:
- We'll provide an allowlist for staging IPs; our infra team will follow up with a short network snippet.
- Prioritize the accurate variant for prompt quality; we can run a quantized variant in a follow-up quick pass.
- We'll send a small set of sample prompts and a staging API key via our secure channel (Tom will handle).

Adding links: HubSpot deal (https://hubspot.example.com/deals/ACME-1423) and a DocuSign SOW link (https://app.docusign.com/ACME-POC-SOW).

Appreciate the quick turnaround — can you share the updated runbook and the throughput matrix before EOD tomorrow?

Best,
Lara

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Lara Chen <lara@acmehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 21 Sep 2028 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC kickoff + hands-on load window (requirements & availability)

Great — confirmed: Oct 3 13:00–15:30 PST (hands-on) and Oct 4 09:00–12:00 PST (load window).

Agenda (draft) — please comment/edit:
- 13:00–13:20: introductions & success criteria (agree SLOs: p95 < 300ms, throughput baseline 150 req/s)
- 13:20–14:00: prompt review & routing (sample prompts from Acme)
- 14:00–14:30: runbook walkthrough (staging access, keys, run triggers, rollback)
- 14:30–15:00: instrumentation and metrics (what we'll capture: per-route latency, GPU utilization, KV cache hit rates)
- 15:00–15:30: open Q&A / next steps (post-load analysis plan)

Load window plan highlights for Oct 4: steady-state 3x 10-minute runs at 150 req/s, plus two 60s spike tests to 300 req/s. We'll execute using the Redwood test harness; Dylan will orchestrate and stream metrics to the shared dashboard. Success criteria: no p95 violations > 300ms for steady-state runs, and graceful degradation (no system outages) during spikes.

I've attached the updated runbook and throughput matrix for your review: POC-Runbook-v2.pdf, throughput-matrix.xlsx. Please confirm the staging allowlist once available and we'll create ephemeral keys for the test window.

Thanks — I'll send a calendar invite with conferencing and the shared dashboard link shortly.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: POC-Runbook-v2.pdf, throughput-matrix.xlsx
